title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for the 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. The previous and next pages characterise, for a k-module A, the functorial maps Hom_k(A,M) → Hom_k(A,Γ^p M), written f ↦ f^{(p)}. Such maps correspond to elements u_p ∈ Hom(A, Γ^p A) with u_0 = 1, u_1 = id and Δ(u_p) = Σ_{i+j=p} u_i⊗u_j. They should also correspond to functorial PD structures on Hom_k(A,J) ⊂ Hom_k(A,B), for every PD-algebra (B,J). This page, headed 'Deux questions de p.d.', isolates the questions behind that equivalence.

(1) Let A be a coassociative coalgebra, presumably cocommutative so that convolution is commutative. Let (B,J) be a k-algebra with a PD ideal, e.g. (Γ^•M, Γ^+M). Then Hom_k(A,B) is a k-algebra under convolution f*g = μ∘(f⊗g)∘Δ, and Hom_k(A,J) is an ideal in it.
- If A is free of finite type, Hom_k(A,B) = Ǎ⊗B with ideal Ǎ⊗J = J·(Ǎ⊗B). This ideal has PD, because Ǎ⊗B is free, hence flat, over B, and PD structures extend along flat base change.
- Question: does the ideal Hom_k(A,J) carry PD in general?
- Modern answer: yes when A is cocommutative and the iterated coproduct A → (A^{⊗n})^{S_n} = TS^n(A) lifts to Γ^n(A), which is automatic for A flat. Put f^{[n]} = γ_n ∘ Γ^n(f) ∘ Δ^{(n)}, where γ_n : Γ^n(J) → J is induced by the PD structure.
- Over a field one can also argue via the fundamental theorem on coalgebras: A is the union of finite-dimensional subcoalgebras A_i, so Hom(A,B) = lim Ǎ_i⊗B, and the PD structures pass to the limit.

(2) Take B = Γ^•A, J = Γ^+A, and let u_1 ∈ Hom_k(A,B) be the identity A = Γ^1A. Put u_n = u_1^{(n)}, the divided powers of u_1 in the convolution algebra. Two questions:
- Do they satisfy γ^A_{pq} ∘ u_{pq} = Γ^p(u_q) ∘ u_p, where γ_{pq} : Γ^{pq}A → Γ^pΓ^qA is the map x^{[pq]} ↦ (x^{[q]})^{[p]}?
- Are they the only elements with u_1 as given satisfying this relation together with u_p u_q = c_{pq} u_{p+q} (c_{pq} the binomial coefficient)?
These are exactly the PD axioms (x^{[q]})^{[p]} = c x^{[pq]} and x^{[p]}x^{[q]} = binom(p+q,p) x^{[p+q]}, transported to coalgebra-side data. They say that u = Σ u_n is a 'group-like / exponential' universal element. The u_n are the coproduct iterates lifted to Γ^n, so the first relation reduces to coassociativity and cocommutativity.

(3) Dual situation: A is a (commutative associative) algebra and B is a coalgebra with a 'coproduit à division' relative to the cokernel of a subcoalgebra B' → B. The example is B = Sym^•M with B' = Sym^•(0) = k. Then Hom_k(B,A) is an algebra with PD on Ker(Hom_k(B,A) → Hom_k(B',A)). For B = Sym M this recovers Hom(Sym M, A) ≅ completed Γ(M^∨)⊗A-type algebras, whose augmentation ideal has PD.

Purpose: to set up a Yoneda-style description of divided powers (Γ as a functor and its universal elements). Such a description is used to build PD envelopes and the PD de Rham complex functorially.
errors: The transcription's 'Hom_k(A,M) a une structure d'anneau' must read Hom_k(A,B); in the image the letter is probably B.
Commutativity (and hence a PD structure in the usual sense) requires A to be cocommutative; the page says only 'cogèbre associative', unless the heading's 'commutatif' covers it.

Over a general base k one needs the iterated coproduct to land in Γ^n(A) rather than merely in TS^n(A). This is automatic only for A flat, so the general answer to question 1 depends on this extra hypothesis, which is not stated.

ideas.what: PD structure on the convolution algebra Hom_k(A,J) ⊂ Hom_k(A,B) for A a cocommutative coalgebra and (B,J) a PD algebra; finite free case via Ǎ⊗B and flat base change
ideas.modern_name: divided powers on convolution algebras / PD extension along flat maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; flat extension of PD due to Berthelot (1974); convolution viewpoint in Hopf/formal group theory

ideas.what: Coalgebra-side encoding of PD axioms: u_p : A → Γ^p A with Δ(u_p) = Σ u_i⊗u_j, u_p u_q = binom·u_{p+q}, γ_{pq}u_{pq} = Γ^p(u_q)u_p, as a universal (Yoneda) characterisation of functorial PD on Hom(A,-)
ideas.modern_name: coalgebras over Γ / divided-power coalgebra structures; exponential (group-like) elements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby (polynomial laws, Γ); Fresse and others for operadic divided powers

ideas.what: Dual: algebra A and coalgebra B with 'divided' coproduct relative to a subcoalgebra B' (e.g. Sym M), giving PD on Ker(Hom(B,A) → Hom(B',A))
ideas.modern_name: duality Sym ↔ Γ (graded dual of Sym is Γ); PD on dual algebras of cocommutative coalgebras

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a clean characterisation problem: functorial PD structures on Hom_k(A,J), for all PD algebras (B,J), are equivalent to coalgebra-type data u_p : A → Γ^p A satisfying exponential and composition relations. He also asks about uniqueness of the u_n. The answer is the general (non-flat base) notion of a 'Γ-coalgebra' as opposed to a TS-coalgebra. This dichotomy is visible in later operadic work (Fresse's Γ(P,-)), but this coalgebra-side version is not standard.
missed.quote: Sont-ils (avec u_1 posé) les seuls éléments satisfaisant cette relation plus u_p u_q = c_{pq} u_{p+q}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is relevant to divided-power coalgebras over non-flat bases and to derived/animated PD structures, where the Γ-versus-TS distinction is essential. It gives a Yoneda-style definition of PD convolution algebras.

deep.surprise_reason: Natural and largely folklore questions (PD on convolution algebras, the Sym/Γ duality). The Yoneda-style characterisation is neat but expected, and was left as questions.
